evidence.text: At fixed discrete flux data, solve holomorphicity for complex structure and zero-FI calibration for Kähler geometry. Positivity selects the physical branch. Charged scalar contributions require a different calibration equation and cannot be omitted from stacks that rely on Higgsing.

sources.title: D-brane Deconstructions in IIB Orientifolds

evidence.text: Represent D7s by a holomorphic tachyon T:E′→E, E′=σ*E*, with support detT=0. The worldvolume bundle is obtained from the quotient (E/TE′)|Σ tensored with KΣ^(−1/2). Cofactor equations locate flux-dual curves; polynomial counting and quotienting by bundle automorphisms yield moduli and matter.

evidence.text: Construct Dirac zero modes by mixing internal spinor components when oblique fluxes obstruct single-component solutions. Establish the proposed basis through field equations, torus transition laws, and orthonormality integrals using Fourier and Gaussian sums.

destination.question: How can gravitational propagation and background diagnostics constrain or distinguish specified gravitational EFTs observationally and theoretically?
destination.summary: Keeps relative wave speeds, time advances, KK signatures, polarization, quasinormal spectra and global chronology as separate tests.

systems: Deformed GR backgrounds and observational surveys
targets: Propagation relative to a specified matter metric
Comparative accessibility of circular closed timelike curves
assumptions: The leading speed-sign argument uses its stated positivity assumptions and matter conditions
Absence of a resolvable time advance and global chronology are different diagnostics
conventions: Relative matter–gravity propagation is distinguished from a coordinate or field-frame speed
Low-energy group or effective-cone speed is distinguished from front velocity
includes: Prospective observations and comparative consistency tests
excludes: A universal sign for every curvature correction and background
Equating low-energy superluminality with demonstrated acausality
Claiming all-frequency isospectrality from an eikonal question
Treating an observational agenda as an established measurement

evidence.text: Integrate out massive matter and expand the local effective action in derivatives. Appendix A uses perturbative graviton one-, two-, and three-point diagrams with dimensional regularization for a massive scalar; coefficients for spinors and vectors are imported from prior effective-action calculations.

evidence.text: GW standard sirens combine an amplitude-derived luminosity distance with source redshift. Bright sirens use electromagnetic counterparts; dark sirens can use statistical host identification. The distance calibration assumes GR, so the stated model independence concerns freedom from a cosmic distance ladder.

sources.title: Isospectrality in Effective Field Theory Extensions of General Relativity

evidence.text: Linearize an action R+L(Riemann) with a geometric-optics perturbation hμν=eμν exp(iΦ). The dispersion calculation uses derivatives of L with respect to Riemann and four-dimensional identities from antisymmetrization over five indices to remove polarization dependence for the selected quartic combination.

sources.title: Global causality constraints in rotating scalar-tensor spacetimes

evidence.text: For a fixed 2π-periodic axial generator, test its invariant norm gφφ. Supplement gφφ>0 by ΔK=gttgφφ−gtφ²<0. In the assumed circular metric class and where gφφ>0, the latter is equivalent to gtt of the inverse metric being negative, making t a local time function.

sources.title: Speed of gravity

evidence.text: Use metric field redefinitions, forward elastic matter-scattering amplitudes, and spin-0/spin-2 Källén–Lehmann spectral representations to investigate coefficient signs. The gravitational forward-limit bounds require additional assumptions about the massless graviton pole and dispersion-relation subtractions.

sources.title: Speed of gravity

evidence.text: Reduce higher time derivatives perturbatively using lower-order equations or field redefinitions, remove momentum-dependent friction, and organize a two-time-derivative hyperbolic equation with perturbative higher spatial derivatives. The authors interpret this organization as resumming secular terms in the retarded Green's function.
